record_reviews.summary: Hooker writes from Darjeeling about Falconer, Hodgson, Himalayan collecting, Sikkim/Nepal access, geology, soils and glacial questions, then labels a long block as Hodgson’s answers to Darwin’s queries. Those answers cover European seed fertility, domestic hybrids (Axis/Juraol, Yak/Bos), fowl and dogs, deer, silk moths and a disputed inheritance anecdote; the letter closes with route/health and correspondence requests.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 13 Oct 1848. The body contains a clear attribution boundary at P12: Hooker says the following answers are Hodgson’s, not his own. Keep those paragraphs as reported Hodgson evidence, not Hooker voice.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Hooker authors the letter; P13-P22 are explicitly attributed answers from Hodgson. Separate CD pencil annotations and cover note “Coal Paper” are scholarly marginalia, not composition.

evidence.quote: The following answers to your queries are all His not mine, they were all news to me
Do not forget to make enquiries about origin, even if only traditionally known of any vars. of domestic quadrupeds, birds, silkworms &c.

record_reviews.summary: Hooker’s travel continuation describes Sikkim’s ridges, rivers, terraces, red clay, route through the Teesta and Kinchin, snowfields, glacial deposits, transported boulders, lake beds and rock structure, ending with his return and request to forward the letter to Lyell.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 3 Feb 1849; this is explicitly a continuation of a Nepal journey described in a separate letter to Lyell, which Lyell will forward to Darwin.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Hooker’s 22 paragraphs are complete; the CD cover annotation asks a later geological question and is not Hooker prose.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: No direct Darwin prompt is identified in the surviving text. The companion 1220 is a separate letter of the same date, not assumed to be a continuation edge.

record_reviews.summary: Hooker continues the 3 February correspondence with a personal and editorial discussion: he received Darwin’s 6 October letter, asks Darwin to preserve speculative letters, discusses Hodgson pamphlets and Ross’s cattle-hunt extract, requests possible Athenaeum extracts, comments on barnacle supplemental males and Darwin’s nomenclature campaign, and reports Falconer/Colvile difficulties and his own high-altitude illness.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 3 Feb 1849; it explicitly records receipt of 1202, while “continuation” belongs to the separate travel letter 1219 and cannot be used to merge their bodies.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Hooker’s 12 paragraphs are complete; passages about Ross’s publication and his father’s letters are Hooker’s report of external material.

evidence.quote: On my return I received your’s of Oct. 6th. for which very many thanks.
pray thank Mr Hodgson cordially for me for the pamphlets

record_reviews.summary: Darwin responds to Hooker’s long Indian report with questions about Blyth and domestic breeds, challenges the wild Bhil/domestic fertility report, discusses altitude distribution and insular floras, and develops his cirripede species argument before family and scientific news.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s nine paragraphs are complete; reported Blyth/Hodgson material is not an embedded voice.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Context already read in batch03; retained here for source completeness, with no duplicate new relation.

record_reviews.summary: Hooker briefly acknowledges Darwin’s excellent letter, promises a fuller Hodgson-based answer, reports recovery from illness, reacts to the barnacle-sex discovery, and appends a Darjeeling elevation note.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Signed 24 July 1848; P5 is an appended Darjeeling note, not a new assumed composition date.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Hooker’s five paragraphs survive; editorial notes identify 1174 as the antecedent and distinguish the appended mountain measurement.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Context already read in batch03; no duplicate relation proposed.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin answers Hooker’s health note, thanks Hodgson for pamphlets, discusses his cirripede work and supplemental males, praises Hooker’s botanical summaries in Ross, and asks after Falconer.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially [6 Oct 1848]; the body explicitly responds to Hooker’s tiny note but retains no physical receipt date.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s six paragraphs are complete; Ross and Hodgson references are reported sources.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Context already read in batch03; 1220 explicitly identifies this letter as received.

proposed_links.reason: Hooker explicitly labels P13-P22 as answers to Darwin’s queries and says the facts were new to him. Darwin’s P3 requested enquiries about domestic varieties, birds and silkworms; Hooker’s attributed Hodgson block supplies exactly those categories, including domestic hybrids and fowl. Scope is limited to the attributed answer section; Hooker’s own Himalayan report is not duplicated as a reply.
proposed_links.response_scope: 1203 P12-P22, especially the explicitly attributed Hodgson answers; no single physical receipt date assigned.

proposed_links.reason: Hooker explicitly says he received Darwin’s 6 October letter. P2 answers Darwin’s concern about Hooker’s health and P3 addresses Hodgson pamphlets sent in the October mail; the later paragraphs also answer Darwin’s nomenclature and barnacle topics. This is a direct response independent of the same-day 1219 travel letter.
proposed_links.response_scope: 1220 P2-P7, with P1-P4 specifically tied to 1202; later personal matters are separate.

issues: 1203 has a critical authorial boundary: Hodgson’s answers are explicitly reported as “all His not mine.”
1219 and 1220 share 3 February 1849 but are separate letters; 1219 is a travel continuation while 1220 explicitly answers 1202.
1219 says a separate Nepal letter to Lyell will be forwarded to Darwin; that missing/other endpoint is not treated as read or as a prompt.
